name: Ad account audit for waste and growth (Meta first)
asked_as: where am I wasting money on ads
my ROAS dropped, what's wrong with the account
we're taking over this ad account, review it
can our ads take more budget
is our agency doing a good job
outcome: The owner knows, in money, what the ad account is losing now, what is stopping them from seeing the truth, and the few changes to make first, ranked by gross profit gained for the effort. Each finding shows its evidence and its fix, nothing in the account was changed, and every fix waits for their yes.
first_principles: Work in this order: tracking, then structure, then spend against return, then creative. A winner chosen on a doubled or missing Purchase event is not a winner, and a budget call on it moves money on a wrong number.

Waste is measured in gross profit, not ROAS. Spend is wasted when its purchases times gross profit per purchase come to less than the spend. Break-even ROAS (order value divided by gross profit per purchase) is the line; an account average above it hides segments, placements and ads far below it.

Platform-reported ROAS over-counts against store orders: view-through credit, existing customers who would have bought anyway and catalog retargeting all inflate it. Reconcile Meta purchases with store orders week by week and read new-customer revenue per ad spend before calling anything a winner or advising more budget.

Fragmentation is a silent tax. An ad set needs about 50 purchases in 7 days to leave learning; an account split into many small ad sets pays more per purchase than the same money in a few funded ones, and every edit restarts the clock.
Cheap clicks are not cheap. Clicks, traffic and engagement objectives, and placements where clicks rarely become page views, inflate CTR and teach delivery to find clickers instead of buyers.

Read only. The audit never changes the account: no pauses, budget edits, new audiences or test events. Every fix is a proposal with money at stake, how easily it can be undone and a review date, and the owner approves each one.

questions.ask: What does one typical order leave you after product, shipping, fees and returns, or what cost per purchase do you aim for?
questions.why: Without it no ad set can be called a loser or a winner, and no finding can carry money at stake.

options.label: I'll give the number
options.con: often forgets shipping, fees or returns

options.label: Work it out from my costs
options.con: needs cost per item in the store

options.label: Use my target cost per purchase

questions.default: Work it out from product costs and the order export with store-meta-math; until then run only the tracking and structure checks and give no kill or money figures
skip_if: brief or brand brain gives gross profit per purchase or break-even ROAS
questions.settle_with_data: Store products export with cost per item plus the 90-day order export (discounts, shipping, refunds, payment method) give gross profit per purchase by product; check the owner's target cost against it and flag a target above break-even as a finding.

questions.ask: What counts as wasted money to you?
questions.why: It decides which lens ranks the findings: losing money per order, paying for buyers you already had, or spend that does not grow new customers.

options.label: Spend that loses money on the order
options.con: misses spend on people who would buy anyway

options.label: Spend on people who'd buy anyway
options.con: needs store new-customer data to size

options.label: Spend that doesn't bring new customers
options.con: can look harsh on profitable retargeting

questions.default: Rank on the first lens and show the second beside it, since both come from the same exports
skip_if: brief says what the worry is (for example 'retargeting looks too good')
questions.settle_with_data: Compute all three from the exports (spend below break-even; existing-customer spend and frequency; new-customer revenue per ad spend). Ask only if the top three fixes change with the lens.

questions.ask: If we free up money, should it go back into what works or come off your ad bill?
questions.why: It changes the plan from cuts only to cuts plus moves, and whether a scale check is needed.

options.label: Back into what works
options.pro: more profit at the same spend
options.con: needs stock, cash and tracking to hold

options.label: You decide from the data
options.con: one more check before any move

questions.default: You decide from the data: move it to proven winners only where scale-readiness-check passes, otherwise save it
skip_if: brief names a fixed or falling budget
questions.settle_with_data: Stock cover on advertised products, the cash limit and whether tracking passes decide if freed money can be moved safely.

questions.ask: Can I read the ad account and your store orders: a read-only connection, exports, or screenshots?
questions.why: The audit is only as good as what it reads; store orders are what makes it honest.

options.label: Read-only connection
options.con: a few minutes to set up

questions.default: Use the connector if live, read only; otherwise ask once for the 90-day ad-level export with breakdowns, Events Manager screenshots, the activity history and the order export
questions.settle_with_data: Check the connector first. Read access covers the whole audit; never ask for more.

tools: node tools/preflight-meta.mjs context/current-structure.json (the live account written in plan shape; every FAIL is a finding)
look_for: Tracking: Meta 7-day click purchases above store orders means double counting (two pixels, pixel and server without a shared event ID, thank-you page reloads); far below means lost events (consent banner, checkout change, broken app).
Tracking: Purchase without value or currency, a value that does not match the break-even definition (tax, shipping, discount), or a test event code left live sending real purchases to Test Events.
Tracking: low match quality on Purchase from missing hashed email and phone on server events; rank fixes by what they add to the Purchase signal, not to page views.

Attribution: the share of reported purchases from view-through; the gap between default and 7-day click ROAS; in Advantage+ Sales, ROAS on new customers against overall. A big gap means the 'best' campaigns are partly existing demand.
Structure: purchases per ad set per week against about 50; the share of spend in learning-limited ad sets; how many ad sets the budget could actually feed (weekly purchases / 50).

Structure: objective mismatch. Every traffic, engagement, reach or clicks campaign, and every ad set optimising for link clicks or landing page views, on a sales goal goes straight to the waste bucket unless it has a written purpose and cap.
Structure: overlap. Several campaigns selling the same products to the same people in the same country bid against each other and split learning.
Structure: more than one significant edit a week on a core ad set in the activity history; constant tinkering keeps it in learning.
Audiences: prospecting with no purchaser exclusion; 30-day frequency on existing customers far above about 10; catalog and retargeting ads holding a large share of spend.

Spend against return: segments, regions and placements with spend share well above revenue share and ROAS under break-even with enough purchases to trust (15+); and the reverse, underfunded segments returning well above break-even.
Junk clicks: placements where link clicks rarely turn into landing page views (in-stream video, Audience Network); high CTR there is accidental taps, not interest.
Funnel break: the biggest drop between landing page view, add to cart, checkout and purchase. A weak page or checkout is not fixed by ad changes.
Winners: paused ads that beat break-even with 15+ purchases; relaunching them (by post ID) is usually the cheapest gain in the account.
Fatigue: past winners whose last-90-day ROAS fell well below lifetime while frequency climbed; cold ad-level frequency above about 2 is a warning.
Creative depth: distinct concepts live, not files; a few ads holding most of the spend is normal until they tire, then the account has nothing behind them.
Kill rule check: ads and ad sets that spent 3x target cost per purchase with 0 to 1 purchases and still run; judge at ad set level, since ad-level credit is noisy.
Money leaks: spend on products out of stock or nearly so, and bid caps or ROAS goals so tight the campaign barely spends.
Scaling read: the cost of the last extra customers when spend rose, not the average; for cash on delivery, delivered orders, not placed ones.
Not spending: account disabled, payment failed, spending limit, rejected ads, empty product set. Check these before any budget idea.

hypothesis_patterns.pattern: Tracking is doubling or losing purchases
hypothesis_patterns.evidence: Meta 7-day click purchases differ from store orders by more than about 20% over 14 days; no shared event ID; low Purchase match quality
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Fix tracking first and re-read every other finding on store numbers

hypothesis_patterns.pattern: The account is too fragmented to learn
hypothesis_patterns.evidence: most ad sets under 10 purchases a week; large share of spend learning limited; overlapping campaigns
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Consolidate in stages into one prospecting campaign per business split plus a testing lane

hypothesis_patterns.pattern: Money is buying clicks, not buyers
hypothesis_patterns.evidence: clicks or traffic objective on a sales goal; placements with link clicks far above landing page views and few purchases
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Move that spend to Sales optimised for Purchase; exclude the junk placements in manual campaigns

hypothesis_patterns.pattern: Existing customers take the budget and the credit
hypothesis_patterns.evidence: no purchaser exclusion, high frequency on buyers, ROAS on new customers far below overall
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Exclude buyers from prospecting and cap their spend in money; expect reported ROAS to drop and store new-customer orders to rise

hypothesis_patterns.pattern: A segment loses money while another is underfunded
hypothesis_patterns.evidence: spend share far above revenue share under break-even, 15+ purchases; another segment the reverse
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Shift through creative made for the strong segment and exclusions, not narrow targeting

hypothesis_patterns.pattern: Proven winners are off or tiring
hypothesis_patterns.evidence: paused ads above break-even with 15+ purchases; last-90-day ROAS well below lifetime at rising frequency
hypothesis_patterns.bet: Relaunch by post ID with a fresh hook and first frame, and add new formats behind them

decisions.ask: How do we act on the structure findings?

options.label: Consolidate in stages, side by side (my usual pick)
options.pro: results stay steady; old winners pause last with a rollback rule
options.when: some ad sets are at target and tracking passes

options.label: Consolidate in one go
options.when: nothing holds target, or tracking was broken so past learning is worthless

options.label: Leave the structure, cut only the waste
options.when: core ad sets already get about 50 purchases a week at target

decisions.recommend: Staged unless no ad set held target for 7 days. Never within 21 days of a sale or launch. If tracking fails, the first move is the tracking fix and the structure change waits for two clean weeks.

decisions.ask: Where does the money from the cuts go?

options.label: Into proven winners and underfunded segments (my usual pick)
options.con: needs stock, cash and a scale check
options.when: tracking passes and winners have stock for twice their current daily sales

options.label: Save it
options.pro: cash back now; no new risk
options.when: cash is tight, stock is thin, or tracking is unverified

options.label: Into the testing lane
options.when: the account has few proven concepts and fatigue is the main risk

decisions.recommend: From the diagnosis: move it to winners only where scale-readiness-check passes; to the testing lane when creative depth is the bottleneck; save it when tracking or cash fails.

rules: Read only: never pause, edit, create, publish or send test events in the account. Proposals only.
Tracking first: if the store-vs-Meta check fails, it is finding 1 and every money figure is re-read on store orders or marked provisional.
Every finding has evidence (export row, date range or screenshot), money at stake per month with its method, the fix, the effort and whether it can be undone.

Money at stake is gross profit, never revenue: spend below break-even is spend minus purchases x gross profit per purchase. For measurement findings write 'decisions on this much spend a month', never an invented loss.
No verdict on fewer than 15 purchases or less than 3x target cost per purchase spent; mark it 'not enough data'.
Read on 7-day windows; daily swings at low spend are normal.
Rank by monthly gross profit gained divided by effort, inside three buckets: losing money now, blocking measurement, costing growth. Hygiene items that move no money go to an appendix.
The week list has at most five changes, each a yes or no, with its risk (for example 'restarts learning on two ad sets') and a review date.
No 0 to 100 score: a weighted score lets a broken purchase event hide behind good creative.
Say what the data cannot tell, for example true incrementality without a lift test.

preflight: node tools/preflight-meta.mjs context/current-structure.json (findings source: each FAIL is listed)
node tools/preflight-meta.mjs context/proposed-plan.json (any proposed new structure must PASS with zero FAIL)
checks: No finding contradicts the tracking verdict; numbers are the same everywhere they appear.
Not-spending causes were checked before any budget recommendation.
Every change is written as a proposal; nothing is described as done.
senior_review: Did I reconcile Meta purchases with store orders before trusting any ROAS in this audit?
Is every 'waste' figure gross profit lost, with its method, and not revenue or a benchmark?
Which campaigns optimise for something other than Purchase, and did I put their spend in the waste bucket or justify it?
Which ad sets can never leave learning at their budget, and does the fix reduce the ad set count?
Did I check how much of the best-looking ROAS is existing customers and view-through?
Are the top three fixes the biggest gross profit for the effort, or just the easiest to spot?
Can each fix be undone, and does it restart learning? Is that written next to it?
What does the owner need to approve this week, in five items or fewer?

ask: How to reconcile Meta purchases with store orders and spot doubled or lost events
Learning phase volume and the signs of a fragmented account
How much existing-customer frequency is too much
Fatigue and kill-rule thresholds for a store this size
How to put money at stake on each audit finding from the store's own gross profit
Order of fixes: data, structure, creative
Conversions API deduplication, event match quality and test event codes
Attribution setting and reporting basis for a store

never: The owner's margins, spend and results come from their data, never the library; library thresholds are labelled as rules of thumb.

files: AUDIT.md: one screen first: losing money now (top three, gross profit per month each), blocking measurement, this week (five items at most), and can it take more spend: yes, after fixes, or not yet.
Findings table (CSV): rank, bucket, check, finding, evidence, gross profit at stake per month with method, fix, effort, can it be undone, access needed, review date.
Reconciliation table: week, Meta 7-day click purchases, Meta default purchases, store paid orders, new-customer orders, ad spend, new-customer revenue per ad spend.
Ranked action plan by gross profit gained for the effort, with winners to relaunch and kill rules per ad set.
Change list for approval, with the line: I have not changed anything in your account; each change waits for your yes.
Not checked: each missing input and what it would change.
next_moves: Build the fixed structure as a plan that passes preflight (meta-account-structure journey)
Relaunch the paused winners with fresh hooks (creatives journey)
A daily watch that flags fatigue and tracking drift early (ad-early-warning-watch)
The landing page or checkout fix if the funnel break is on the site (cro-audit journey)
